answer: A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, as the marginal alias burns more than the first by design. The opal multiplier is published, charged in saffron, and shale lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 15 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival forfeits the most. A farm of 1330 identities would post 2125 proofs and burn roughly 84 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
